barriers.description: Designers faced resource constraints (funding, space, coordination) that limit the feasibility of implementing prototypes at scale.
barriers.justification: Lack of funding, physical spaces and coordination capacity prevents designers from refining, scaling and evaluating prototypes in real service settings, hindering production of design solutions and iterative testing.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Issues like manicure funding, the provision of physical spaces in waiting rooms, and the coordination of waiting times with medical care should be reviewed.

barriers.description: Healthcare centers lacked capacity to absorb demand induced by the 'Encanto' prototype, constraining designers' ability to test real-world uptake.
barriers.justification: If health centers cannot schedule Pap test appointments in a timely manner, designers cannot validly evaluate uptake or iteratively improve the experience based on real attendance data, hindering evaluation and facilitation of user involvement.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, due to the appeal of the service, the healthcare center must attend to the demand induced by ‘Encanto’ and schedule Pap test appointments in a timely manner.

barriers.description: Older women had difficulty handling touchscreen tablets, reducing designers' ability to include them in usability testing and interactional evaluation.
barriers.justification: Low digital literacy among some participants prevented effective interaction with the app prototype, hindering designers' ability to evaluate designs, understand context of use, and facilitate inclusive user involvement.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The tablet was not an adequate tool for women over 60 years old, who had difficulty handling a touchscreen.

barriers.description: Beacon-delivered messages produced notifications but resulted in few users effectively accessing the linked video, limiting outreach effectiveness.
barriers.justification: Low effective access to the video via Beacons prevented designers from reaching and testing with target users in their contexts, constraining evaluation of the media-based prototype and its iterations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: After analyzing the data, it was determined that, although there were 297 message notifications in the targeted cellphones, few people had effective access to the video.

barriers.description: The project lacked a follow-up mechanism and interoperable information systems to link outreach messages to clinic visits, limiting outcome evaluation.
barriers.justification: Without systems to identify which women were reached and whether they subsequently attended clinics, designers cannot measure effectiveness or integrate feedback for the media strategy, hindering evaluation and management of user understanding.
barriers.reference_excerpt: in order to value the effectiveness of the media-based strategy, a follow-up mechanism must be included that can identify the women outreached with this technology and, subsequently those who visited primary healthcare centers to take a Pap test.

barriers.description: The Citobot required further hardware modifications and additional clinical and AI development before it could match existing devices and be validated.
barriers.justification: Technical limitations (narrower viewing angle) and the need for AI algorithm development and clinical validation prevented designers from finalizing the device and fully evaluating its performance in context, hindering production of robust design solutions and evaluation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, the speculum’s viewing angle was greater than that of the Citobot, so this device requires further modifications in hardware development. ... In subsequent studies, we will advance clinical research to determine the acceptability, reproducibility, sensitivity, and specificity, concordance with cytology, and predictive capacity of the Citobot. At the same time, we will develop the machine learning algorithms of the AI incorporated into this medical device.
